module

public import Mathlib.Analysis.Real.Cardinality

@[expose] public section

open scoped Topology

/--
A sequence `(s_1, s_2, s_3, ...)` of real numbers is said to be equidistributed on
an interval `[a, b]` if for every subinterval `[c, d]` of `[a, b]` we have
`lim_{n→ ∞} |{s_1, ..., s_n} ∩ [c, d]| / n = (d - c)/(b-a)`
-/
def IsEquidistributed (a b : ℝ) (s : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ c d, c ≤ d → Set.Icc c d ⊆ Set.Icc a b →
  Filter.atTop.Tendsto (fun n => ((Finset.range n).filter
    fun m => s m ∈ Set.Icc c d).card / (n : ℝ)) (𝓝 <| (d - c) / (b - a))

/--
A sequence `(s_1, s_2, s_3, ...)` of real numbers is said to be equidistributed
modulo 1 or uniformly distributed modulo 1 if the sequence of the fractional parts of
`a_n`, denoted by `(a_n)` or by `a_n − ⌊a_n⌋`, is equidistributed in the interval `[0, 1]`.
-/
def IsEquidistributedModuloOne (s : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  IsEquidistributed 0 1 (fun n => Int.fract (s n))

findings.description: The definition does not require `a < b`, although interval equidistribution is defined for a non-degenerate interval. This produces substantive bad cases: if `b < a`, no nonempty `Icc c d` can satisfy the containment hypothesis, so every sequence is declared equidistributed. If `a = b`, the predicate instead requires the frequency of the single value `a` to tend to zero, because `(d - c) / (b - a)` becomes `0 / 0 = 0`. Lean-checked examples establish `∀ s, IsEquidistributed 1 0 s`, `IsEquidistributed 0 0 (fun _ => 1)`, and `¬ IsEquidistributed 0 0 (fun _ => 0)`. Present problem-file callers avoid these cases because they use the modulo-one wrapper with endpoints 0 and 1.
findings.source_evidence: Wikipedia, “Equidistributed sequence”, Definition, explicitly says “equidistributed on a non-degenerate interval [a, b]” and normalizes frequencies by its length `b - a`: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equidistributed_sequence#Definition . The module's docstring reproduces this definition but omits “non-degenerate”.
findings.suggested_fix: Require `a < b`, either by defining the predicate as `a < b ∧ ∀ c d, ...` with the existing frequency condition, or by requiring a proof of `a < b` as an argument. Do not silently extend the predicate to empty and zero-length intervals with its current behavior.

findings.description: At the use site `FormalConjectures/Books/UniformDistributionOfSequences/Equidistribution.lean`, the universally quantified parameter and hypothesis `Transcendental ℚ x` assert equidistribution of `x * (3/2)^n` for EVERY transcendental multiplier. This is not the cited problem or metric result. In particular, an almost-everywhere assertion cannot be strengthened to every transcendental parameter: there are transcendental exceptional multipliers. Bugeaud's winning-set result for lacunary real sequences, applied to `t_n = (3/2)^n`, gives a full-Hausdorff-dimension set of multipliers with `inf_n ‖x t_n‖ > 0`. Such a set contains transcendental numbers, and their fractional parts omit an interval of positive length, contradicting equidistribution. This is an unsupported stronger statement at a use site, not a defect in the modulo-one definition or merely a stale tag on the original `(3/2)^n` problem.
findings.source_evidence: Kuipers–Niederreiter, Uniform Distribution of Sequences, Chapter 1, Corollary 4.2 (p. 35), states that `(x^n)` is uniformly distributed for almost all `x > 1`; the discussion on p. 36 asks about the specific sequences `(e^n)`, `(π^n)`, and `((3/2)^n)`, not every transcendental scalar multiple (indexed excerpts: https://books.google.com/books?id=mnY8LpyXHM0C&jscmd=SearchWithinVolume2&q=%22Corollary+4.2%22). Bugeaud, Distribution Modulo One and Diophantine Approximation, Exercise 7.3 and the discussion on pp. 166–167, records that for a lacunary sequence of positive real numbers `t_n > 1`, the set `{ξ : inf_n ‖ξ t_n‖ > 0}` is winning (https://books.google.com/books?id=NeEpoAf7k0IC&jscmd=SearchWithinVolume2&q=%22lacunary%22). The full-Hausdorff-dimension property of winning sets is also explicitly stated in Moshchevitin, arXiv:0812.3998, Introduction.
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the unsupported universal-transcendental variant. If a parameterized metric result is intended, state that `x * (3/2)^n` is equidistributed for Lebesgue-almost every real `x`, supply the corresponding metric-theorem reference, and mark that result solved. The original unscaled `(3/2)^n` conjecture and `IsEquidistributedModuloOne` should not be changed on this account.

reformulations.difference: The Lean definition tests closed intervals, including singleton intervals, and counts indices starting at zero. The usual textbook formulation tests `[c,d)` with `0 ≤ c < d ≤ 1` and starts at index one.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Fractional parts lie in `[0,1)`. Closed-interval equidistribution gives zero limiting frequency to every singleton. Conversely, the half-open tests force zero singleton frequency by bounding a point by arbitrarily short intervals; the point 1 never occurs. The closed count equals the half-open count plus the right-endpoint count, proving equivalence. Starting at zero instead of one changes each normalized interval count by at most `1/n`, so the limiting condition is unchanged. Both equivalences were proved in `/workspace/review/reindex.lean` (`modulo_one_iff_standard` and `modulo_one_shift_iff`), with no `sorry` dependencies.

reformulations.difference: The use-site definition retains only irrational representatives in `(0,1)`, whereas Mendès France defines the full spectrum over `ℝ/ℤ`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Represent the circle by `[0,1)`. The omitted rational representatives, including zero, form a countable set. Consequently the full spectrum is countable exactly when its irrational part is countable. The exact equivalence between `(Bugeaud04.Spectrum x).Countable` and countability of the unrestricted spectrum in `[0,1)` was proved in `/workspace/review/spectrum_use.lean`, using the actual imported use-site definition. Thus this restriction does not change the posed countability problem.

review.notes: Both declarations and all their problem-file use sites were checked. No Mathlib duplicate of either sequence predicate was found; `MeasureTheory.pdf.IsUniform` concerns a different notion. Real division, multiplicity-preserving index counts, negative fractional parts, singleton intervals, and the initial zero index were tested. Successful Lean experiments are in scratch.lean, reindex.lean, and spectrum_use.lean under /workspace/review/. The main equivalence proofs depend only on propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound. Bugeaud was checked through indexed book excerpts; the full page 215 preview was restricted, but Mendès France's primary paper independently supplies the spectrum definition and countability problem. No repository edits were made, and the reviewed module's hash matches its committed version.

submission.summary: Added `a < b` to IsEquidistributed and updated its docstring to require a non-degenerate interval. The required compile command reports no errors or warnings. Separate Lean regression tests confirm that degenerate intervals are rejected and that the original frequency condition, including the modulo-one wrapper, is unchanged on valid intervals.
